title: Lemon Panna Cotta
subtitle: Set cream infused with fresh lemon zest and a splash of limoncello
excerpt: Cream steeped with fresh lemon zest, set with gelatine into a delicate, yielding dome. The limoncello adds a clean citrus finish without making it boozy.
sourceNotes: A citrus variant of the classic Italian panna cotta, well established in British restaurant cooking and home baking books. Lemon zest infusion is a natural extension of the vanilla original; the addition of limoncello is a modern flourish common in British recipe writing from the 2000s onwards.

recipe.batchNotes: Can be made up to 2 days ahead and kept in the moulds in the fridge.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the day before. Turn out just before serving.

content.text: Lemon panna cotta is cream infused with strips of fresh lemon zest, set with gelatine, and turned out into a smooth, barely-trembling dome with a delicate citrus perfume. The limoncello adds a clean, bright finish and a slight alcoholic warmth, leave it out for a more delicate result. The key step is the 20-minute infusion: the zest needs time to release its oils into the warm cream before you strain it out.

items.prepNote: pared zest only, taken in wide strips with a peeler

content.text: Use a vegetable peeler to pare wide strips of zest from the lemons, avoiding the white pith. Add the cream, sugar, and lemon zest strips to a small saucepan and heat gently over a medium-low heat, stirring occasionally, until the cream is steaming and the sugar has dissolved. Do not let it boil. Remove from the heat, cover the pan, and leave to infuse for 20 minutes. Meanwhile, submerge the gelatine leaves in a bowl of cold water and leave for 5 minutes until soft.

Strain the infused cream through a sieve into a clean saucepan, discarding the lemon zest. Reheat gently until just steaming. Squeeze the excess water from the gelatine leaves and drop them into the warm cream. Stir until fully dissolved, about 1 to 2 minutes. Remove from the heat and stir in the limoncello if using. Pour the mixture into lightly oiled ramekins and leave to cool to room temperature. Cover with cling film and refrigerate for at least 4 hours until set.

To turn out, run a thin knife around the inside edge of each ramekin. Place a serving plate on top, invert firmly, and shake gently. The panna cotta should release with a soft wobble. If it sticks, hold the base of the ramekin in warm water for 10 seconds and try again. Serve with a few fresh raspberries or a curl of lemon zest.

items.cause: The infusion time was too short, or the zest was finely grated rather than pared in strips.
items.fix: Wide pared strips give more flavour than fine zest because they release oils more slowly. Infuse for the full 20 minutes, longer if time allows. Do not grate the zest directly into the cream, as fine zest releases more bitter pith compounds.

items.cause: Too much gelatine or it was chilled at very low fridge temperature for too long.
items.fix: Reduce to 2.5 gelatine sheets next time. The set panna cotta should wobble visibly when nudged.

items.symptom: Surface has a skin on top
items.cause: The cream cooled uncovered before refrigerating.
items.fix: Press cling film directly onto the surface of the cream before it cools, or refrigerate as soon as the cream is at room temperature.

content.text: Keeps in the moulds in the fridge for up to 2 days. Once unmoulded, serve within an hour. Do not freeze.
